MENTOR: I can't show you how Hatch Rig moves. My view of this comp tells me which layers follow which, but not whether a null has keys or when they are. If you want to see it, select Hatch Rig in the timeline, press U to show its keys, and scrub through. What I can say is that Hatch follows Hatch Rig, so anything Hatch Rig does to its Position, Scale or Rotation, Hatch does too, on top of its own animation. That's the setup you're about to build.

Tile, Caption and Stamp are now the group.

I tried to show you a frame at 0 s, but the image came back too small to see anything, so I won't describe it. What I can read is that Tile sits in the upper right of the comp at 0 s.

Here's the idea:
- **A parent carries its children.** When a layer follows another, it picks up that layer's Position, Scale and Rotation. It keeps its own animation as well, so if Caption fades in now, it will still fade in.
- **Opacity and effects aren't passed down.** Fading or blurring the parent does nothing to its children.
- **A null never shows in the render.** It's an invisible handle, so it can't add its own look to the group. You put it where the group should turn or scale from and animate it instead of the layers.

Your turn. Add a null with **Layer > New > Null Object**. Then tell me where the group should turn or scale from: a corner, the middle of an edge, or the middle of the group. "It'll only slide" is a fine answer too.
